questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to be in a beautiful city where I could experience Italian everyday life and Bologna seemed to tick off that. Furthermore the University has a long history and the city is located close to hills and with great connections to all of Italy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall a great experience but the academic level in Bologna wasn't very high.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There wasn't much guidance upon arrival only a virtual meeting which didn't provide much information. Furthermore much of the information regarding how to sign up for classes in Bologna would have been useful to get beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only a 30 minutes virtual meeting where a coordinator from Bologna quickly went through the most basic things needed for the stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would have liked the information meeting to be held physical and thus giving incoming students the opportunity to connect at the same time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I booked very early and through Airbnb which I can recommend. it was easy and no hidden cost, deposits or shady renters and contracts.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: it is crucial to start looking for accommodation as soon as you know where you are going to spend your exchange year. I would also recommend signing up for the Erasmus Student network WhatsApp group when looking for accommodation. The link to the group can be found by googling ESN Bologna

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Actually very easy as there is no registration for courses, only for exams. But this information wasn't provided beforehand, so I was worried I wouldn't get the courses I wanted and that had been pre-approved.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You simply just show up to the courses you want to attend and then you can sign up for the exam about a month before the exam and that it is only then you are 'locked'.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to contact the exchange student office for Political science by email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just remember that there are no limit in the number of students attending classes, so you'll get the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses ranged a lot from good academic to almost high school level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is more interactive since in some courses active participation is a part of the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environment in International Politics
International Development Economics
international Relations of East Asia
EU as a global actor

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend International Development Economics as it is very interesting and focuses on development in a broad sense.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, but living in an Italian city means spending a lot on aperitifs, coffee and just food in general

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: there are not many discount supermarkets in Bologna why food is generally more expensive than in Denmark, but local produce is significantly cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think the university had a sports club but no information was provided, so I did not attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university has a large number of museums which are free of charge for students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The hills near Bologna are very much worth a visit and the train will tak you to Milano in 1 hour, Florence in 40 minutes and Rome in 2 hours.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to adjust to the Italian way of life and just remember that everything might be a bit more bureaucratic, but that is just the Italian way.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and talk to the people you have class with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It takes some time to get used to how 'old fashioned' the teacher-student relationsship is.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Italian way of being outside and enjoying the city all year round - Also the food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You do not have to sign up for the courses as places aren't limited. This would have been great to know beforehand.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The professors are very different and the exams thus also differ a lot as there is no general guidelines. So make sure to read into what kind of exam a course has, as some exams are quite small compared to others resulting in the same number of credits.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just being able to have a everyday life in an Italian city for 4 months

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: How to figure out the way the Italian system functions.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do not stress about the exams as the level in Italy generally is lower than at Københavns Universitet.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
